assumptions: East-west and height 77 px per metre, depth 51.25 px of v per metre, as every section (S5). With them the street figures are about 1.3x life, as at the gate and in S6. Diminution (standing or walking adults, head to foot, px): on the street's north margin, foot v 890-975 (D 11.5-13.2 m): the doctor 157, the standing woman 170, the pointing man 179, the visitor 165, the man at the post 164 (leaning), the bucket man 168 (foot v 997); in the street, foot v 1240-1278 (D 5.6-6.3 m): the porter 171, the bundle man 149, the walker with a bag 143, the pale attendant 187, the groom 190, the folded-object bearer 208. Means 167 and 175: no diminution across the street band (the spread within each band is 25 %). The one-scale frame holds here.

Things far up the silk are painted smaller (S7.bld.hall_ns_1620 at about 0.55 of the street's scale, eave about 170 px for a roughly 4 m eave): positions still come from their points, but heights and depths read there are about half of real. The frame keeps one scale (BUILDING.md rule 5); built sizes there are the builder's choice.
Painted figure size is not a scale. Place by foot point.

entities.name: main hall of the official's compound (top of the silk)
entities.what: The compound's main hall at the top of the silk: a long hip-gable (歇山) tiled roof with tile-ends along its eave and its east gable (山花, bargeboards and an ornament) showing; its west end is behind the willows. Under the eave its front is a panel between posts, covered with rows of small dark motifs, with a dark upright rectangle in its lower middle from which a thin curved outline runs out to both sides: either a patterned curtain or screen hung across the open front, gathered by a dark tie or showing a dark doorway behind it, or a patterned wall or lattice window. It is not a board of characters: the motifs are too uniform and evenly spaced. A further post stands east of the panel. No faces are painted at it.

entities.name: gate hall (门屋) of the official's compound 官宦人家
entities.what: The street gate hall of the official's compound: single storey, open to the street under a tiled roof with bracket sets (斗拱) under the eave and a lintel beam over a wide open passage between the west column, which stands on a stone block, and an east post hidden behind the man pointing the way. Inside, a lamp or hook hangs from the lintel in the east part of the passage (u ~1337), and a small dark-topped shape shows at the edge of the open door leaf (u ~1248: S7.fig.face_at_gate_door_1251, a peeking head or a small lamp, one thing); the west half of the passage holds a light door leaf standing open against the west jamb, with a ring-knocker dot, and at the back of the passage a low railed partition (the lower half of a back door, or a screen) stands under a post. West of the passage is a plain-walled west bay, where the gatekeeper sits, with a slatted panel high under its eave (a rolled bamboo blind or a lattice); a low dark-hatched panel (a door leaf folded back?) stands on the block against the west pier. No board or writing is painted on it.
